doc.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26

title: Louis's blues and the song Sister Kate
summary: Manetta recalls Louis in 1917 and the numbers Wine and Grind and Sister Kate, and how they were published elsewhere under other names.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So when I came back to town, Joe had went to Chicago. Well, in 1917, Lewis was just playing three numbers. That's right. He played in the audience, he was a blues. He made a number called Wine and Grind. He named them. Sister Kate. Well, Sister Kate, take your finger out of Kattie's head. And then, of course, Joe Oliver and Jane Crying Swim, AJ P. Ron, take the number, went to New York and had it published as Sister Kate.
No, my mama's baby boy. Huh? I and my mama's baby boy. I've never seen the music. I've been trying to find it, but I can't find it in a place.
Sister Kate. Wasn't it Sister Kate? No.
Sister Kate was take your finger out of Kattie's head. Yeah. And they named it, If I Could Sheep Me Like My Sister Kate. Yeah. And C. Ron and Trance Williams.
That's right. They did publish that other thing with the...
But Wine and Grind was something about mama's... They named it different up there, I don't know what you call it.
